falsifier: the free model names an open fact with no place in the model as a question kind, or its entries are free text by choice rather than by a broken emission
hypothesis: a free OpenRouter model can stand in for the deployed critic model when the question-kinds prompt is measured, at no cost
intervention: E9's Qwen replay read again, entry by entry. E9 counted 9 attribute-name subjects; that was a misreading. Each of the 9 facts appears twice in the same verdict: once as a sound element_id and attribute reference, and once with the same element_id and attribute plus subject set to the attribute's name and assertion set to '}],', which is schema punctuation inside a string. A schema-constrained decoder cannot write that, so the endpoint did not constrain the output to the schema. OpenRouter lists structured_outputs for this endpoint but not response_format, and its documentation says some endpoints treat a schema as a strong hint. Corrected figures: 9 facts with a place in the model, each sound, each with a broken duplicate; 1 fact without a place ('rate or size limits'), written as a subject where capacity-limits fits; 0 typed. Whether the model saw the kinds' descriptions is not known, because the forwarded request is not visible
